notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR11 (kb/Work PB5382, landed): every line a REPLACE introduces takes the indicator of the line the replaced text begins on: CopyProcessor.ApplyReplacements writes the debugging-line carrier on each introduced line when that line is a debugging line, and drops the carriers pseudo-text-2 wrote when it is a source line (ResultRule.KeepsPseudoTextDebuggingLines false, asked with EditionInfo.ReplacedTextIsLaidOutInFixedForm), so DebuggingLineRewriter keeps or hides every introduced line. A literal placed on a debugging line that the program-text area cannot hold from its area's margin (65 positions in area A, 61 in area B) draws COBOL7039. Witnesses: pb5382-replace-debugging-introduced-lines (1, ONE, TWO, THREE at 85), pb5382-replace-literal-on-debugging-line (COBOL7039), 1985-GR-XII_3_4-11 (the long literal on a source line still runs).

next.reason: 1985: "the indicator area of the introduced lines contains the same character as the line on which the text being replaced begins"; 2023: "shall be in logical free-form reference format. Text-words inserted ... are placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format". Same subject, placing inserted text, but 2023 uses logical free-form: no indicator area, no added continuation lines, no error for a literal continued onto a debugging line.
